name: Hashabiah
overview: Hashabiah was a male Levite, specifically a descendant of Aaron, serving as a priest during the post-exilic period. He is uniquely identified as the son of Hilkiah, which situates him within the priestly lineage responsible for temple service. His role as a priest underscores the continuation of Aaronic duties among the Levites after the return from exile.
namesAndTitles: The name Hashabiah means 'YHWH has reckoned,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning tied to God's sovereignty. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 12:21, was not given directly by God but carries a strong covenantal implication consistent with priestly service.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hashabiah was the son of Hilkiah, establishing his direct lineage within the priestly family. Beyond this father-son relationship, no additional family connections are noted in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Hashabiah's significance lies in his role as a priest descended from Aaron, serving in the post-exilic community as noted in Nehemiah. His identification as Hilkiah's son places him within the restored priesthood, emphasizing the faithfulness of God's covenant through the preservation of the Levitical line. This continuity was vital for reestablishing proper worship and temple practices among the returned exiles.
